title: Fish Amritsari
subtitle: Spiced fried fish from Amritsar
excerpt: Fish Amritsari is a street food from the city of Amritsar in Punjab. Pieces of white fish are coated in a spiced yoghurt batter and deep-fried until golden and crisp. It is sold from roadside stalls and eaten with chutney and sliced onion.
sourceNotes: Amritsar in Punjab is famous for its street food. Fish pakora -- spiced fried fish -- has been sold near the Golden Temple for generations. The batter is distinctive for its use of gram flour and ajwain (carom) seeds, though this version uses cumin as a substitute.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The fish can be marinated and coated up to 2 hours ahead. Fry just before serving.

content.text: The fish must be very dry before coating -- pat each piece firmly with kitchen paper. The batter should cling and coat rather than drip. Fry in small batches and keep the oil hot between batches.

items.prepNote: cut into 5cm chunks, patted very dry
or use gram (chickpea) flour for a crispier result

content.text: Mix the yoghurt, garlic paste, ginger paste, cumin, turmeric, chilli flakes, and salt in a bowl. Add the flour and mix to a thick paste.
Add the fish pieces and toss to coat completely. Cover and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a deep saucepan to 180 degrees. Test with a small piece of bread -- it should turn golden in 30 seconds.
Fry the fish in batches of 4 to 5 pieces. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and crisp. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain on kitchen paper. Keep warm in a low oven while you fry the remaining batches.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges and a green chutney or sliced raw onion.

items.symptom: Batter falls off in the oil
items.cause: Fish was not dry enough or oil was not hot enough
items.fix: Pat the fish very dry before coating and make sure the oil reaches 180 degrees before frying
Fry in smaller batches and allow the oil to return to temperature between each batch

items.symptom: Outside is golden but fish is raw inside
items.cause: Pieces are too thick or oil too hot
items.fix: Cut fish into 3cm chunks for more even cooking and reduce heat slightly

content.text: Amritsar is one of the great food cities of India. Fish Amritsari sits alongside kulcha and lassi as the dishes that define the city's street food identity. It is sold near the Golden Temple and in the narrow lanes of the old city, eaten standing up with chutney from a small paper cone.
